lectures.title: Parliament: Houses, Rajya Sabha, constituencies and presiding officers

parts.t: Components of Parliament and the Council of States
items: **Parliamentary Components:** Parliament consists of President + Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha.
**Vice-President:** ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha, but is NOT a constituent member of Parliament.
**"Council":** the term "Council" in Indian Polity spans three distinct constitutional institutions; one is the Council of States (Rajya Sabha): Upper House of the Union Parliament (Art. 80).
**Nature:** Permanent House; NOT subject to dissolution; 1/3rd of members retire every 2 years.
**Member Tenure & Age:** Member's term is 6 years; minimum age is 30 years.
**Strength Limits:** Maximum sanctioned strength = 250 members: 238 representing States/UTs + 12 nominated by the President.
**12 nominated members:** nominated by the President for expertise in Literature, Science, Art, and Social Service.
**Electoral System:** State representatives are elected by the elected MLAs of State Legislative Assemblies via Proportional Representation by Single Transferable Vote (PR-STV) under secret ballot.
**Who cannot vote:** Nominated MLAs and MLCs cannot vote.
**Allocation of seats:** based on population (not equal).

parts.t: How the two Houses are elected
items: Directly by citizens registered in territorial electoral rolls
Plurality wins (Candidate does NOT need 50%+ votes)
Elected MLAs of the respective States
Nominated MLAs and MLCs cannot vote; Allocation based on population (not equal)
**First Lok Sabha General Elections:** 25 Oct 1951 – 21 Feb 1952; total 489 seats contested; first Speaker: G.V. Mavalankar.
**Smallest Constituency by Area:** Chandni Chowk, Delhi (10.59 sq km).
**Area vs Electorate Size:** Ladakh is the largest constituency by geographical area, while Chandni Chowk is the smallest by area.
**Largest State Representation:** Uttar Pradesh (80 Lok Sabha Seats).
**Single-Seat States/UTs (1 Seat):** Sikkim, Mizoram, Nagaland, Chandigarh, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Puducherry.
**Two-Seat States (2 Seats):** Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Manipur, Meghalaya.

parts.t: Presiding officers of the two Houses
items: **Rajya Sabha Chairman (Arts. 64 & 89(1)):** The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States.
**The Universal Trap:** The Chairman is NOT a member of the Rajya Sabha.
**Deputy Chairman (Art. 89(2)):** Chosen from amongst the sitting members of the Rajya Sabha (IS a member).
**Lok Sabha Speaker (Art. 93):** Elected by the Lok Sabha from amongst its members.

parts.t: Presiding officers: oath, resignation and removal
items: **No separate oath:** The Speaker and Deputy Speaker take NO separate oath of office as presiding officers (they take oath solely as ordinary Members of Parliament).
NO SEPARATE OATH (oaths taken only as MP)
Resolution of Lok Sabha by Effective Majority (Art. 94; 14 days' notice)
NO SEPARATE OATH (oaths taken only as MP)
Resolution of Lok Sabha by Effective Majority (Art. 94; 14 days' notice)
NO SEPARATE OATH (oaths taken only as MP)
Resolution of Rajya Sabha by Effective Majority (Art. 90; 14 days' notice)
**Speaker & Deputy Speaker Reciprocal Resignation (Art. 94(b)):** Speaker resigns to the Deputy Speaker (NOT to the President); Deputy Speaker resigns to the Speaker (NOT to the President).

**Removal Notice Threshold (14 Days):** Removal of President (Art. 61), Lok Sabha Speaker/Deputy Speaker (Art. 94), and Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman (Art. 90) all require at least 14 days' advance written notice.
**Leader of Opposition (LoP) Recognition:** First formally recognized in 1969.
**Numerical Threshold:** The largest opposition party must hold ≥ 10% of the total House strength (approx 55 seats in Lok Sabha).
**Summoning:** The President calls each House of Parliament to meet under Article 85; the maximum gap between two sessions cannot exceed 6 months.
**Maximum Parliamentary Session Gap:** 6 Months under Article 85 (implies a minimum of 2 sessions per year); Parliament must meet at least twice a year.
**Session:** The period between the first sitting of a House and its prorogation or dissolution (Standard sessions: Budget, Monsoon, Winter).
**Sitting:** A daily meeting of the House during a session (comprises morning and post-lunch sittings).
**Recess:** The period between the prorogation of a session and the commencement of a new session (e.g., when Parliament is in recess, the President may issue ordinances under Art. 123).
**Adjournment:** Terminates a daily sitting for a specified time (hours, days, or weeks); exercised by the Presiding Officer (Speaker/Chairman).
**Adjournment Sine Die:** Terminating a sitting without assigning a day for reassembly.
**Prorogation:** Terminates a session of the House (not the House itself); issued by the President under Article 85(2).
**Dissolution:** Ends the life of the House entirely; applies only to Lok Sabha (Rajya Sabha is a permanent House).
**Quorum:** The minimum number of members required to be present to conduct official business.
**Constitutional Quorum:** 1/10th of total membership of the House (Art. 100).
Adjournments exceeding 4 consecutive days and prorogation periods are excluded from the 60-day limit.
Consideration of Money Bill by Rajya Sabha
Money Bill deemed passed if not returned within 14 days.
Art. 101(2); Prohibition of Simultaneous Membership Rules, 1950
Failure to resign State seat in 14 days vacates Parliament seat.
Notice for RS Deputy Chairman removal
Vacation of seat due to MP Absence
If an MP is absent from all House meetings for 60 days without permission, the seat may be declared vacant.
Parliament must meet at least twice a year.
**14 Days:** always associate with the Rajya Sabha Money Bill detention limit (Art. 109).
**14 Days:** always associate with resolving dual membership between Parliament and State Legislature.
**14 Days:** always associate with the removal notice for Presiding Officers (Speaker / RS Deputy Chairman).

lectures.title: Parliament: Question Hour, Zero Hour and parliamentary questions

parts.t: Hours as tools of executive accountability
items: **Purpose:** Parliamentary hours and procedural motions serve as the primary mechanisms through which Parliament enforces executive accountability and scrutinizes government policies.
**Parliamentary Accountability Triangle:** Question Hour + Supplementary Questions + Adjournment Motions directly ensure executive responsibility to the legislature.
**Interpellation:** The formal procedural right of asking questions to demand explanations of government actions or policies from the Executive.
**Question Hour:** The first hour of every sitting dedicated to asking and answering questions.
**Zero Hour:** An Indian parliamentary innovation (since early 1960s) following Question Hour to raise urgent public matters without prior formal notice.
**Indian Innovations:** Both Zero Hour (early 1960s) and Calling Attention Motion are indigenous contributions to parliamentary practice.
Asking and answering questions addressed to Ministers
Starred, Unstarred & Short Notice rules apply
Immediately follows Question Hour (12:00 Noon – 1:00 PM)
Raising urgent matters of public importance without prior notice
**11:00 AM – 12:00 Noon:** Question Hour in Lok Sabha ↔ Zero Hour in Rajya Sabha.
**12:00 Noon – 1:00 PM:** Zero Hour in Lok Sabha ↔ Question Hour in Rajya Sabha (post-2014).
**1 Hour:** Maximum duration of Zero Hour in Lok Sabha.
**Context:** Raised during Question Hour (the first hour of every parliamentary sitting) to ensure executive accountability.
**Addressed To:** Primarily addressed to Ministers to scrutinize administrative policies and government actions.
**Three Primary Categories:** Starred, Unstarred, and Short Notice Questions.
**When taken:** Starred, Unstarred and Short Notice Questions are all taken during Question Hour.

parts.t: Starred vs Unstarred vs Short Notice Questions
items: Oral Answer on the floor of the House
Written Answer laid on the Table
**Starred Question:** Requires an Oral Answer; Supplementary questions CAN be asked; Maximum 20 oral questions listed per day.
**Unstarred Question:** Member does not require an oral answer in the House; purely Written Answer; NO supplementary questions permitted.

**Short Notice Question:** Must relate specifically to a matter of urgent public importance; accepted with a shorter notice duration than ordinary questions; addressed orally, Supplementary questions permitted.
**Daily Starred Questions Limit:** Maximum 20 oral questions listed per day in Lok Sabha.

lectures.title: Parliament: motions, special rules and financial procedure

items: Tests majority support of Council of Ministers
50 Members (Governed by Rule 198); no reasons required
Proves majority support on the floor
Moved by the Council of Ministers / Government
Expresses strong disapproval/criticism of specific policies
**No-Confidence Motion:** Moved by the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (Rule 198); moved only in Lok Sabha; needs 50 members' support; no reasons required.
**No-Confidence Motion, consequence:** If passed, the Government must resign.
**First No-Confidence Motion:** 1st moved by J.B. Kripalani (1963) against Nehru.
**Confidence Motion, consequence:** If defeated, the Government falls.
**Censure Motion:** Moved against an individual minister or entire council; does not force immediate resignation, but demonstrates political weakness.
**50:** Minimum members required to support the admission of a No-Confidence Motion.

parts.t: Calling Attention, Adjournment and Privilege Motions
items: Draws a Minister's attention to an urgent public matter
Suspends normal business for a definite urgent matter of public importance
Raised against a Minister for withholding/distorting facts
**Calling Attention:** Indian innovation; does NOT contain an element of censure/condemnation; restricted scope of Adjournment Motion.
**Adjournment Motion:** Carries an element of censure/condemnation; interrupts normal business.
**Privilege Motion:** Referred to Committee of Privileges.
**Closure Motion:** A motion moved to cut short debate and put the matter directly to vote.
**Guillotine:** A specific form of closure where, upon the expiry of allotted time, all undiscussed clauses or demands for grants are put to vote immediately.
**Closure (Guillotine):** Puts all undiscussed financial demands/clauses to vote; Lok Sabha; on expiry of allotted debate time; closes debate immediately; undiscussed business voted upon.
**Rule 184 (Lok Sabha):** Permits discussion on a matter of public interest accompanied by a formal motion and voting (If defeated, ruling party faces potential collapse).
**Rule 377 (Lok Sabha):** Allows members to raise urgent matters not covered under Questions, Calling Attention, or other motions; written notice to Secretary-General.
**Rule 377, daily limit:** 20 matters are allowed to be raised on a day.
**Yielding the Floor:** The parliamentary convention where the Speaker orders a speaking member to yield/stop to allow another member to speak.
**Annual Financial Statement:** Constitutional nomenclature for the Union Budget under Article 112.
**Appropriation Bill (Art. 114):** Statutory authorization enabling withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India for voted grants and charged expenditure.
**Vote on Account (Art. 116):** Advance grant given by Lok Sabha to cover estimated expenditure for a part of the financial year pending budget passage.
**Vote of Credit:** An unexpected, blank-check financial grant for an emergency or indefinite demand whose details cannot be stated in a budget.
**Charged Expenditure:** Non-votable expenditure paid directly out of the Consolidated Fund of India (can only be discussed).

parts.t: The three Cut Motions (Demands for Grants)
items: Complete disapproval of the underlying policy
Reduce the demand by a specified amount
Demands economy in expenditure; aims at achieving administrative economy
Ventilates a specific grievance within the Government's sphere of responsibility
**Cut Motion Amounts:** Policy Cut = ₹1 | Token Cut = ₹100 | Economy Cut = Specified amount.
**Consequence:** The passage of any Cut Motion in Lok Sabha signals loss of financial control and obliges the Government to resign.
**Role:** Parliamentary Committees act as a primary mechanism of parliamentary control over administration, handling detailed and complex legislative scrutiny.
**Standing Committees:** Permanent and continuous; reconstituted annually or periodically (e.g., Financial Committees, DRSCs).
**Ad-hoc Committees:** Temporary; constituted for a specific inquiry/task and cease to exist after submitting their report (e.g., Joint Parliamentary Committees, Inquiry Committees).
**Department-Related Standing Committees (DRSCs):** Total 24 DRSCs: 16 under Lok Sabha + 8 under Rajya Sabha (Standard Joint ratio approx 2 : 1).
Scrutinizes CAG Audit Reports, Appropriation Accounts & wasteful expenditure
Examines budget estimates; suggests economy & administrative efficiency
Scrutinizes PSU accounts, commercial soundness & PSU-related CAG reports
**PAC Chairman:** appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha; by convention since 1967, the Chairman is selected from the Opposition.
**Estimates Committee Chairman:** appointed by the Speaker (traditionally from the ruling party).

**Estimates Committee:** Rajya Sabha has zero representation; it is the single largest parliamentary committee (30 members, strictly from Lok Sabha). Always eliminate options suggesting Rajya Sabha members.
**CAG Report Examination:** Examined primarily by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) as well as the Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU) for PSU audits.

**Committee on Subordinate Legislation:** Examines whether delegated executive rule-making (regulations, bye-laws, sub-rules) stays within statutory limits (15 members in each House; Ministers barred).
**Committee on Government Assurances:** Tracks and reports on the fulfillment of promises, undertakings, and assurances given by Ministers on the floor of the House.
**Committee on Petitions:** Examines petitions and representations submitted to the House (Lok Sabha: 15 members; Rajya Sabha: 10 members; Ministers barred).
**Business Advisory Committee:** Regulates the official parliamentary timetable and programme of House business.
**Rules Committee:** Recommends amendments, additions, and procedural adjustments to the Rules of Procedure.
**Ethics Committee (Lok Sabha):** First constituted as Ad-hoc on 16 May 2000; made permanent in 2015; oversees moral/ethical member conduct; cannot take up sub-judice matters.
**Consultative Committees:** Constituted by the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs (not parliamentary committees per se); MPs from specific zones/ministries are members.

parts.t: Ministers and committees; the 2G Spectrum JPC
items: **Minister Membership Trap:** Ministers CANNOT be elected/nominated to Financial Committees (PAC, Estimates, COPU), Committee on Subordinate Legislation, or Committee on Petitions.
**2G Spectrum JPC (2011):** 30 Members (20 Lok Sabha + 10 Rajya Sabha); chaired by P.C. Chacko (Ad-hoc Joint Committee).
